subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Thanks for taking the time today, Alex — really appreciate the candid conversation. Below is a short recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can move toward a scoped POC. If I missed anything, flag it and I'll update.

Pain points you shared:
- Unit economics: current cost per 100M tokens is higher than expected; pressure from execs to reduce inference spend by ~50-70%.
- Latency at peak traffic causing timeout/retries (esp. during batch scoring windows).
- Ops overhead running mixed stack (managed APIs + in-house GPU cluster) and lack of visibility into token-level cost.

Current stack (as discussed):
- Primary model: in-house LLM inference (BLOOM variant) on dedicated cloud GPUs for low-latency endpoints.
- Fallback: third-party hosted API for burst traffic and embeddings.
- Infra: Kubernetes + custom autoscale scripts; currently no automated KV/prefix caching in front of the model.

Success criteria you mentioned:
- 2–3x reduction in cost per 100M tokens (target range: 40–60% savings) while maintaining comparable quality.
- P95 latency under 250ms for interactive routes; predictable cost at scale.
- Clear rollout plan with canary strategy and ability to toggle quantized serving if quality delta acceptable.

Where Redwood can help (initial hypotheses):
- Quantized model variants + kernel-level optimizations to reduce GPU token cost. You indicated openness to trying 8-bit / 4-bit quantized weights for non-critical routes.
- Automatic batching + KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts to lower per-token compute.
- Smart routing: use dedicated pools for baseline traffic and hosted fallback for bursts to avoid overprovisioning.
- Transparent token-level billing so you can see breakdowns by route/model.

Immediate next steps:
1) I've attached a short pricing/opsheet that maps expected unit economics across a few serving configurations (Redwood-Pricing-opsheet.xlsx) — please confirm the sample QPS and average seq lengths and I'll produce a tailored cost model.
2) Technical deep dive with your infra/ML team to map current inference stack -> propose POC plan (30-45 mins).
3) POC scope: demo quantized model serving + batching/cache config on a representative route; measure latency/quality/cost over 1 week.

Proposed owners:
- Redwood: Ben Carter (cc'd) will run the technical POC.
- FinBot: your infra/ML lead to supply sample prompts, seq-length distribution, and security checklist items.

Attachments: Redwood-Pricing-opsheet.xlsx, POC-playbook.pdf

Thanks — I'll follow up with a couple of times for the deep dive (copying Ben).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks for the clear recap, Marissa — that's exactly the right summary. A few quick clarifications:
- We're definitely open to quantization on non-customer-facing routes; for critical customer flows we need to validate quality first.
- Security is a hard requirement: we need SSO/SAML + SOC2 evidence before any POC that touches production data. Can Ben or someone share the SOC2 summary and what data redaction options are available?
- For the cost model, I'll get you seq length distribution and sample prompts by EOD tomorrow.

Available for a tech dive next week: Tue 2/17 or Thu 2/19 after 10am PT.

Appreciate the quick turnaround here — Alex

Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800

Great — thanks Alex. Quick responses inline and a couple calendar options below.

- Quantization: understood on the prod-sensitive routes. We'll run head-to-head quality evals (same prompt set) during the POC so you can see delta and decide route-by-route.
- Security: Ben will share a SOC2 summary and a short checklist for POC data handling. For the POC we recommend using a synthetic or redacted subset of prompts if you prefer to avoid production data.
- Cost model: appreciate you sending the seq distribution — once we have it I'll run three scenarios (baseline, quantized, quantized + caching).

Calendar options for the tech deep dive:
- Tue 2026-02-17, 11:00-11:45 PT
- Thu 2026-02-19, 10:30-11:15 PT

Ben will lead the technical session (infra + runtime mapping). If one of those works, I'll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Next steps action items:
- Alex: share seq-length distribution + sample prompts (EOD 2/13) — FinBot
- Ben: share SOC2 summary + POC data handling checklist (EOD 2/13) — Redwood
- Marissa: produce tailored cost model once seq stats are in (2/14) — Redwood

Thanks again — looking forward to the deep dive.

Best,
Marissa
